statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail falls to 14% because Friday's close resolved the preceding danger window benignly and the market is now shut: the 30,737.07 cash session low held, NDX finished 209.60 below an intraday record, NQ settled 233.25 under its own session high, and VIX closed 0.01 above its session low.
recommendation: Tail drops seven points to 14%, leaving the watch band, so the mapped policy state moves to EA_ON and Tail sits well below the block threshold. The escalation condition published for the 20:00-21:00Z window was a decisive loss of the 30,737.07 cash session low. It did not occur; that low held into the bell and the index closed 70.86 above it. Two independent retracement facts now stand on the record: cash NDX ended 209.60 under its intraday record high and 61.21 under its own open, and NQ December futures settled 31,049.00, some 233.25 below their 31,282.25 session high. Volatility decayed with them, VIX closing 15.31, down 6.59%, within a cent of its session low. CME equity futures then halted at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, so every one of the 24 published forecast hours falls inside a closed market with no tradable price path. Tail is therefore published in the low band throughout, while Stress stays high at 74% on an energy and conflict backdrop the market cannot price until the halt ends. No danger window is published, because no evidence-based interval inside these 24 hours carries a distinguishable path risk. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: CME closes the week with NQ at 31,049.00 and cash NDX at 30,807.93, both well below session highs, and VIX down 6.59% to 15.31, easing Tail to 14% into a full weekend halt
body:
Cash NDX closed 30,807.93 (+306.37, +1.00%) from a 30,869.14 open and a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range. The index touched an intraday record during the session but did not close at one: it finished 209.60 points, 0.68%, under its own high and 61.21 under its open, while holding 70.86 above the 30,737.07 low that the preceding assessment named as the escalation trigger. NQ December futures settled 31,049.00 (+288.50, +0.94%) on a final 20:59:58Z print, inside a 30,760.25-31,282.25 range from a 30,771.25 open on 573.48k contracts, 233.25 below their own session high. Both legs of the market therefore ended the week retracing rather than extending, which is the structure that argues against a pathological no-retracement path.

Volatility confirmed it. VIX closed 15.31, down 1.08 or 6.59%, from a 16.15 open and inside a 15.30-16.24 range, settling a single cent above its session low. The macro trigger was the September Employment Situation, released at 12:30Z: nonfarm payrolls rose just 29,000 against expectations near 90,000, the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%, average hourly earnings rose 0.1% on the month and 3.0% on the year, and revisions cut July to -10,000 and August to 133,000. Markets read it as removing a near-term tightening risk, with the implied probability of an October rate hike falling from 64% to 16%.

The cross-asset picture is not uniformly calm, which is why Stress stays high while Tail falls. The long end did not follow the front end: the 10-year yield finished about 5.28%, up roughly 4 basis points on the day after initially falling on the payroll print, and the 30-year held near 5.63%, with the 10-year having peaked above 5.34% earlier in the week, its highest since 2002. The H.15 release dated 2 October, carrying 1 October data, shows 2-year 4.78%, 10-year 5.24% and 30-year 5.61%. Energy remains a live shock: WTI eased 1.73% to $91.217 and Brent held $102.58, but WTI is still about 49.8% above a year ago and diesel prices are at record highs. The G7, coordinating with the IEA, announced a release of up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude over four months, with a large portion inside 20 days. Middle East conflict continues behind that, with reported additional U.S. deployments and an intensifying Saudi-Houthi campaign around the Red Sea, where the Houthis reported 94 Saudi strikes in 24 hours.

The decisive fact for the published forecast is structural: CME equity futures halted at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday. The whole 24-hour window runs inside that halt, Saturday carries no scheduled U.S. macro release, and the reopen itself falls outside the window. Tail measures the risk that mean reversion fails against a persistent one-way path, and a closed market provides no path at all, so Tail decays into the single digits mid-window and ends at 12% rather than reaching zero, the residual standing for weekend headline accumulation that can only reprice after this window closes. The shared Finviz context was not used: the file is about 70 hours old with a partial collection status, so it was treated as unavailable and the assessment rests on independent research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available, covering the 21:00Z hour on 1 October through the 20:00Z hour today. Tail ran from 20% to 27% across the window. It opened at 20% and held that watch floor for ten consecutive hours through the U.S. Thursday afternoon and the whole Asian session, then stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z on the European-morning advance, before returning to 20% at 10:00Z and 11:00Z. The 12:30Z payroll release drove the only escalation of the window: Tail reached 24% at 12:00Z, crossed into the elevated band at 25% for the 13:00Z hour and peaked at 27% at 14:00Z, the two hours spanning the release and the 13:30Z cash open, which published orange and BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. It then de-escalated as fast as it rose, back to 22% by 15:00Z and holding 22-23% for the rest of the cash session before easing to 21% at 20:00Z. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 74% and 79%, and Confidence held 88-89%. Dominant mode was mixed for 19 hours with trend-up published for the 08:00Z and 09:00Z European advance and for the 12:00Z through 14:00Z payroll reaction. The window is therefore a complete record of a large labor-market surprise that briefly lifted Tail into the block band and then resolved without producing a persistent one-way path.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 14% for the current 21:00Z hour, seven points below the preceding hour, because the Friday close resolved the prior danger window benignly and the market then shut. Cash NDX ended 209.60 below an intraday record and NQ settled 233.25 under its session high, with VIX a cent off its own low, so retracement and volatility decay are both on the record. The structural fact governing the remaining 23 hours is that CME equity futures halted at 21:00Z and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, which is after this window ends. No published hour contains a tradable session and Saturday carries no scheduled U.S. macro release, so Tail is published in the low band throughout: it eases through the Friday evening hours, settles at a 9% floor across the deep Saturday stretch from 06:00Z to 12:00Z, then drifts back to 12% by 20:00Z as the plausible distribution of the unobserved Sunday open widens. That drift is explicitly conditional and gap-shaped; no halted hour can establish the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail is built to detect. Stress is published between 70% and 74%, easing as Friday's volatility decay carries forward and firming late as the G7 release timetable, the Saudi-Houthi campaign and reported U.S. deployments stay unpriced. Confidence decays from 86% to a 76% floor, remaining in the high band because coverage of index, futures, volatility, yields, energy and the seven-day calendar is complete and verified; what ages is the price path, not the research. Mode is published as mixed for the three hours still shaped by Friday's cross-asset conflict and normal for the 21 hours in which no market structure exists to classify. No danger window is published and the mapped policy state is EA_ON for all 24 hours. The first scheduled high-impact checkpoints, ISM Services on 5 October and the FOMC minutes on 7 October, sit beyond the window.
